reasons.text: Indeed, Will Osula was forced off at half time after twisting his ankle and is now a major doubt for Monday night, so Yoane Wissa should be restored to the number nine role.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).

But we are going to find another solution like we did with Tyrone Mings the last 10 minutes.” – Unai Emery on Aaron Wan-Bissaka WISSA UP FRONT As for Newcastle, Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) played up front here, with Matias Fernandez-Pardo (£6.0m) deployed on the right.

After three goals, an assist and 25 points over the latest two Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Gameweeks, Everton’s Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is currently the second most-bought player of this international break.

Barry’s goals took him to double figures across all competitions for the campaign, with only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) having struck more Premier League goals this season than Barry (six).
Asked about his strong form, Barry told evertontv : “I'm very happy because it's always a pleasure to score and I'm so happy to do my first assist in the Premier League.
BARRY FRONT AND CENTRE Above: Everton players sorted by shots and big chances (BC) in Gameweek 10 It was the usual mix of the sublime and the ridiculous from Barry.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.
Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.
Just four minutes after falling behind, the in-form Barry powered an emphatic header beyond Rushworth after meeting Mykolenko’s looping far-post cross.

And five minutes later, Barry turned the contest completely in Everton’s favour with a scrappy goal, bundling the ball over the line from Tyrique George ’s deep delivery before a VAR review confirmed the effort despite Coventry’s handball claims.

The Blues moved into fifth in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches, having to come from behind to Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener courtesy of a quickfire double from Thierno Barry, before the Frenchman turned provider to see Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall seal the win nine minutes from time.

reasons.text: Indeed, Will Osula was forced off at half time after twisting his ankle and is now a major doubt for Monday night, so Yoane Wissa should be restored to the number nine role.

Goals from William Osula (£5.8m) and Harvey Barnes (£6.1m) secured the points, although the biggest FPL talking point came before kick-off, with Yoane Wissa (£6.1m) and Malick Thiaw (£5.0m) both benched.
Matthias Jaissle made five changes to his starting XI, with Wissa, Thiaw and Sven Botman (£5.0m) among those dropping to the bench.

While it may be tough to ditch Wissa before he faces Crystal Palace on Sunday, there are no guarantees that he will continue in a number nine role at Selhurst Park, particularly with Will Osula (£5.8m) building his fitness.

You get the feeling that things could quickly unravel for Newcastle if they fall behind, too, so there are surely safer bets than Wissa for the upcoming period, like Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) and Nicolas Jackson (£6.6m).

After three goals, an assist and 25 points over the latest two Fantasy Premier League (FPL) Gameweeks, Everton’s Thierno Barry (£5.7m) is currently the second most-bought player of this international break.

Barry’s goals took him to double figures across all competitions for the campaign, with only Erling Haaland (nine) and Alexander Isak (seven) having struck more Premier League goals this season than Barry (six).
Asked about his strong form, Barry told evertontv : “I'm very happy because it's always a pleasure to score and I'm so happy to do my first assist in the Premier League.
BARRY FRONT AND CENTRE Above: Everton players sorted by shots and big chances (BC) in Gameweek 10 It was the usual mix of the sublime and the ridiculous from Barry.

The Toffees fell behind shortly after the half-time interval at Hill Dickinson Stadium, before a brace from Thierno Barry and a well-taken strike by Dewsbury-Hall sealed a third consecutive win in the space of eight days.
But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton 's favour.
Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.
Just four minutes after falling behind, the in-form Barry powered an emphatic header beyond Rushworth after meeting Mykolenko’s looping far-post cross.

And five minutes later, Barry turned the contest completely in Everton’s favour with a scrappy goal, bundling the ball over the line from Tyrique George ’s deep delivery before a VAR review confirmed the effort despite Coventry’s handball claims.

The Blues moved into fifth in the Premier League table ahead of this weekend's round of matches, having to come from behind to Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute opener courtesy of a quickfire double from Thierno Barry, before the Frenchman turned provider to see Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall seal the win nine minutes from time.

reasons.text: Neither Myles Lewis-Skelly nor Ezri Konsa featured in midweek- the former due to suspension and the latter due to injury - but both are expected back in the matchday squad in the Spanish capital.
Konsa joined Arsenal from Aston Villa during this summer’s transfer window, with the England international costing around £55m.
Hill gets his chance after Ezri Konsa was ruled out for Thursday’s Nations League game against Croatia.
Arsenal defender Konsa picked up a small injury in the Gunners' recent Champions League win over Slavia Prague, but he was fit enough to return against Hull City a few days later.
Konsa was originally expected to start for England at Wembley on Thursday evening, but the Three Lions released a statement on Tuesday morning confirming that he was out of contention.
The Three Lions say that Konsa will miss the game as “he continues to follow his own programme”.
Ezri Konsa starts for the Gunners after a brief midweek fitness scare.
CB: Cristhian Mosquera — With Ezri Konsa suffering an injury midweek and William Saliba unlikely to be immediately restored to the starting XI, Arteta might turn to Mosquera this weekend.
Konsa only lasted 62 minutes in the Champions League clash on Wednesday.
